questions.prompt: Which 13th-century theologian's philosophy was later commended by Pope Leo XIII as a model for Catholic teaching?
choices: St. Thomas Aquinas
St. Augustine of Hippo
St. Anselm of Canterbury
St. Bonaventure
questions.explanation: Leo XIII's 1879 encyclical Aeterni Patris held up Aquinas's synthesis of faith and reason -- worked out inside the new university system level 12 just described -- as a lasting model for Catholic philosophy and theology.
questions.hint: His massive theological synthesis is still studied in seminaries today.

citations.quote: restore the golden wisdom of St. Thomas, and to spread it far and wide for the defense and beauty of the Catholic faith

questions.prompt: St. Thomas Aquinas's major work synthesizing faith and reason is called the Summa ____.
questions.explanation: The Summa Theologiae remains one of the most influential works of Catholic theology, systematically working through the whole of Christian doctrine -- and it was written, taught, and debated inside the university system level 12 just introduced.
questions.hint: It's the same theologian named in the previous question's encyclical.

citations.quote: the Fathers of Trent made it part of the order of conclave to lay upon the altar, together with sacred Scripture and the decrees of the supreme Pontiffs, the Summa of Thomas Aquinas, whence to seek counsel, reason, and inspiration.

questions.prompt: St. Anselm of Canterbury, writing a century before Aquinas, summarized theology's basic task in a phrase often translated as what?
choices: Faith seeking understanding
Reason replacing faith entirely
Faith with no role for reason at all
Understanding that requires no faith whatsoever
questions.explanation: Anselm's phrase, 'fides quaerens intellectum,' captures the whole scholastic project this level covers: reason is not opposed to faith but works from within it, seeking to understand more deeply what is already believed.
questions.hint: Faith comes first in this phrase, and reason follows, working from inside it.

questions.prompt: True or False: Scholastic theologians like Aquinas structured their major works around a formal method of stating objections before answering them.
questions.explanation: True. The Summa Theologiae's own structure -- an article poses a question, lists objections, then answers each in turn -- is not incidental decoration; it is the scholastic method itself, disputatio, taking objections seriously rather than ignoring them.
questions.hint: Look at how the Summa Theologiae itself is actually laid out, article by article.

questions.prompt: The scholastic method of formally debating a theological question -- stating objections, then resolving them -- is known in Latin as the ____.
questions.explanation: This method grew directly out of the university classroom level 12 just introduced -- a real, structured practice of public academic debate, not simply a private way of writing.
questions.hint: The Latin word this method is named for, sharing a root with the English word 'dispute.'

questions.prompt: St. Bonaventure, a leading Franciscan theologian and near-contemporary of Aquinas, represents what alongside Aquinas's Dominican approach?
choices: A distinct Franciscan scholastic tradition, showing Scholasticism was never a single uniform school of thought
A complete and total rejection of Aquinas's entire method by the whole Franciscan order itself
An identical theology with no meaningful differences from Aquinas's own theology at all
A separate tradition existing entirely outside the university system this level has already described
questions.correctAnswer: A distinct Franciscan scholastic tradition, showing Scholasticism was never a single uniform school of thought
questions.explanation: Bonaventure, minister general of the Franciscans, developed real theological emphases of his own alongside Aquinas's Dominican synthesis -- a useful reminder that 'Scholasticism' names a shared method and setting, not one single, uncontested set of conclusions.
questions.hint: Consider which order this Franciscan theologian belonged to, alongside Dominican Aquinas.

citations.quote: The personal charism of some witnesses to God's love for men has been handed on... so that their followers may have a share in this spirit... In their rich diversity they are refractions of the one pure light of the Holy Spirit.

questions.prompt: Match each figure or term of Scholasticism to what it represents.

pairs.right: 'Faith seeking understanding,' theology's basic scholastic task
The formal method of stating and resolving objections
The Dominican synthesis of faith and reason in the Summa
A distinct Franciscan scholastic tradition alongside Aquinas's

questions.explanation: Together these show Scholasticism as a real intellectual movement with real internal diversity -- a shared method and setting (the university, the disputatio) producing genuinely different theological schools, not one single voice.
questions.hint: Two of these are individual theologians from different orders; two are the shared method and its motto.

questions.prompt: True or False: Scholasticism treated reason as a threat to faith that needed to be suppressed.
questions.explanation: False. Anselm's own motto -- faith seeking understanding -- already states the opposite: reason works from within faith, deepening it, not undermining or replacing it. This is the same confidence in reason's compatibility with faith that later shapes Leo XIII's own commendation of Aquinas.
questions.hint: Recall Anselm's own motto from earlier in this level.

questions.prompt: What institution, described in the previous level, made large-scale scholastic debate and teaching like Aquinas's and Bonaventure's practically possible?
choices: The medieval university
The monastery alone, with no other institution involved
The royal court of the reigning king
The papal curia in Rome, acting alone
questions.explanation: Scholasticism did not happen in a vacuum -- it is, in a real sense, the intellectual product of the university system level 12 introduced, where mendicant friars like Aquinas and Bonaventure taught, debated, and wrote.
questions.hint: This is the same institution level 12 just described in detail.

questions.prompt: Even as Scholasticism was flourishing at the height of the medieval university system, what real institutional crisis was quietly building within the papacy itself?
choices: A series of pressures that would soon move the papacy to Avignon and later split it between rival claimants
No institutional tension of any kind existed within the papacy during this entire period
The papacy had already permanently relocated to Constantinople by this point
The office of the papacy itself had been formally abolished
questions.correctAnswer: A series of pressures that would soon move the papacy to Avignon and later split it between rival claimants
questions.explanation: Intellectual flourishing and institutional crisis run side by side in this period -- the next level turns from Scholasticism's confident synthesis to a genuinely painful chapter: the Avignon Papacy and the Western Schism.
questions.hint: This is exactly what the next level in this topic covers.

questions.prompt: From 1309 to 1377, where did the papacy actually reside, rather than in Rome?
choices: Avignon, in France
Constantinople
Milan
Jerusalem
questions.explanation: For nearly seventy years, under heavy French political influence, a series of popes governed the Church from Avignon rather than Rome -- a real institutional crisis, not a minor administrative detail, and a stark contrast to the intellectual confidence of level 13's Scholasticism.
questions.hint: This is a city in southern France, not in Italy.

questions.prompt: St. Catherine of Siena, a laywoman with no formal theological education, is remembered for what documented action regarding the Avignon Papacy?
choices: Writing to and personally urging Pope Gregory XI to return the papacy to Rome
Founding the first Dominican convent in France
Serving as an official court theologian to the King of France
Translating the whole Bible into Italian
questions.correctAnswer: Writing to and personally urging Pope Gregory XI to return the papacy to Rome
questions.explanation: Catherine's letters and personal visits are historically documented and credited with helping persuade Gregory XI to end the Avignon Papacy and return to Rome in 1377 -- a specific, traceable action, not a vague reputation for wisdom.
questions.hint: Her persistent correspondence and personal visits are a real, documented factor in a pope's actual decision.

citations.quote: Mary is the perfect Orans (pray-er), a figure of the Church.

questions.prompt: Catherine of Siena's letters contributed to Pope Gregory XI's decision to return the papacy to ____ in 1377, ending the Avignon period.
questions.explanation: This is a rare case where a single laywoman's spiritual authority, exercised through nothing more than persistent letters and personal visits, had a concrete, traceable effect on the papacy's own institutional history.
questions.hint: The city the papacy had been absent from for nearly seventy years.

questions.prompt: True or False: The papacy's return to Rome in 1377 immediately and completely resolved the institutional crisis of this period, with no further complications.
questions.explanation: False. Within a year, disputed elections produced rival claimant popes -- the Western Schism -- meaning the return to Rome actually opened a new and even more confusing chapter rather than closing the crisis.
questions.hint: Consider what happened almost immediately after Gregory XI's return, in the very next papal election.

questions.prompt: At its worst point, how many men simultaneously claimed to be the true pope during the Western Schism?
choices: Three
One
Five
Two dozen
questions.explanation: By 1409, competing elections and failed attempts to resolve the dispute had produced three simultaneous claimants -- a scandal that made the question of legitimate authority urgently practical, not merely theoretical, for ordinary Christians trying to know which pope to obey.
questions.hint: Competing elections eventually produced more than two rival claimants.

questions.prompt: Match each figure or event of this level to what it involved.

pairs.right: The papacy residing in France, not Rome, for nearly seventy years
A laywoman whose letters helped bring the papacy back to Rome
Rival claimants simultaneously claiming to be the true pope
The council that finally resolved the schism and elected one pope

questions.explanation: This whole sequence -- exile, a laywoman's intervention, schism, and finally a council's resolution -- is one continuous institutional crisis, not four unrelated events, stretching across roughly a full century.
questions.hint: Follow the crisis in order: where the papacy went, who helped bring it back, what went wrong next, and how it was finally fixed.

questions.prompt: True or False: John Wycliffe's teachings, condemned at the Council of Constance, included a denial of transubstantiation.
questions.explanation: True. Wycliffe denied that the Eucharistic bread and wine truly become Christ's Body and Blood, and also attacked papal authority and Church-authorized interpretation of Scripture -- positions the Reformation would echo more than a century later.
questions.hint: This is the same Eucharistic doctrine Trent would later reaffirm, in a level still ahead.

questions.prompt: Jan Hus, influenced by Wycliffe's ideas, was summoned to the Council of Constance under a promise of safe conduct. What actually happened to him there?
choices: He was condemned for heresy and burned at the stake in 1415
He was fully exonerated and reinstated to his teaching position
He successfully defended every one of his teachings before the council
He was quietly released and allowed to return home unharmed
questions.correctAnswer: He was condemned for heresy and burned at the stake in 1415
questions.explanation: Hus's execution, despite the promised safe conduct, left lasting bitterness in Bohemia and fed a Hussite movement that persisted for generations -- a foretaste of how explosively unresolved reform grievances could turn, a full century before Luther.
questions.hint: His fate at Constance, despite an official promise, left lasting bitterness in his homeland.

questions.prompt: The Council of ____ (1414-1418) finally resolved the Western Schism, deposing or accepting the resignation of the rival claimants and electing a single pope, Martin V.
questions.explanation: The same council that condemned Wycliffe and executed Hus also, in its central and most lasting achievement, finally ended decades of confusion over who the true pope actually was.
questions.hint: The German city this whole council, and its resolution of the schism, is named after.

questions.prompt: Having just resolved one severe institutional crisis at Constance, what does the Church face barely a century later, in the very next level of this topic?
choices: The Protestant Reformation, met with the Church's own response at the Council of Trent
A second, entirely identical Western Schism with new rival papal claimants
A complete and permanent dissolution of the papal office itself, once and for all
No further institutional or doctrinal challenges of any real kind whatsoever
questions.correctAnswer: The Protestant Reformation, met with the Church's own response at the Council of Trent
questions.explanation: The unresolved grievances Hus's execution left simmering -- clerical corruption, unclear authority, popular anger -- did not simply disappear once Constance ended the schism; they resurface, on a much larger scale, when Luther posts his theses roughly a century later.
questions.hint: Consider what unresolved tensions from this level might still be simmering a century later.

citations.quote: [Each church shall] maintain, educate religiously, and train in ecclesiastical discipline a certain number of youths of their city and diocese.

questions.prompt: The Council of Trent (1545-1563) was convened by the Catholic Church primarily in response to what?
choices: The Protestant Reformation
The Great Schism of 1054
The Investiture Controversy
The Islamic conquest of Spain
questions.explanation: Trent clarified Catholic doctrine on Scripture, grace, and the sacraments against Reformation-era challenges, while also reforming clerical discipline and education -- the direct answer to the crisis level 14 left simmering.
questions.hint: This 16th-century movement, started by Luther, is what Trent was responding to.

citations.quote: [Each church shall] maintain, educate religiously, and train in ecclesiastical discipline a certain number of youths of their city and diocese.

questions.prompt: In 1517, what action did Martin Luther take that is traditionally remembered as sparking the Reformation?
choices: Posting Ninety-Five Theses criticizing the sale of indulgences to the door of Wittenberg's church
Personally assassinating a reigning pope in an act of open rebellion
Founding an entirely new university system across the German lands
Leading an organized armed uprising directly against the ruling Holy Roman Emperor himself
questions.correctAnswer: Posting Ninety-Five Theses criticizing the sale of indulgences to the door of Wittenberg's church
questions.explanation: Luther's theses, intended as an academic challenge to debate, spread rapidly thanks to the printing press and ignited a movement far larger than Luther himself initially intended -- the beginning of the crisis Trent will spend the rest of this level responding to.
questions.hint: This is a specific, documented act of academic protest, not a military one.

citations.quote: [Each church shall] maintain, educate religiously, and train in ecclesiastical discipline a certain number of youths of their city and diocese.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Council of Trent affirmed that both Sacred Scripture and Sacred Tradition hand on divine revelation.
questions.explanation: Against the Reformation principle of Scripture alone, Trent taught that revelation comes to the Church through both Scripture and Tradition together -- a direct doctrinal answer, not simply an administrative one, to the Reformation's core claim.
questions.hint: Trent rejected the Reformation idea that revelation flows through only one of these two sources.

citations.quote: [The Synod] receives and venerates with an equal affection of piety and reverence all the books both of the Old and New Testament... as also the said traditions.

questions.prompt: Against the Reformation principle of 'sola fide' (faith alone), the Council of Trent taught that justification involves what?
choices: A real, interior transformation by grace, received through faith working together with love, not faith alone
Something earned entirely by good works alone, without any need for grace whatsoever
A change that happens automatically at birth for every single person without exception
A state that, once received, can never afterward be lost under any circumstance
questions.correctAnswer: A real, interior transformation by grace, received through faith working together with love, not faith alone
questions.explanation: Trent's Decree on Justification taught that grace truly renews and sanctifies the believer inwardly -- not merely God treating a sinner as righteous while nothing actually changes within.
questions.hint: Trent insisted something real actually changes inside the believer, not just a legal declaration.

citations.reference: Council of Trent (1545-1563), Decree on Justification
citations.quote: If any one saith, that by faith alone the impious is justified; in such wise as to mean, that nothing else is required to co-operate in order to the obtaining the grace of Justification... let him be anathema.

questions.prompt: Match each figure of the Catholic Reformation to their contribution.

pairs.right: Clarified doctrine and reformed clergy in response to the Reformation
Founded the Society of Jesus to renew the Church
Reformed the Carmelite order and wrote on mystical prayer
Implemented Trent's reforms as Archbishop of Milan

questions.explanation: The Catholic Reformation was not only a response to Protestant challenges but a genuine renewal of holiness and discipline within the Church herself, alongside Trent's own doctrinal and disciplinary work.
questions.hint: One founded a religious order, one reformed Carmelite life, one implemented reforms as an archbishop.

citations.quote: [Each church shall] maintain, educate religiously, and train in ecclesiastical discipline a certain number of youths of their city and diocese.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Council of Trent required the founding of seminaries to improve the education and discipline of parish priests.
questions.explanation: Trent's reforms directly addressed widespread clerical ignorance and laxity by mandating formal seminary training for future priests -- the exact institutional gap level 14's crisis had left exposed for generations.
questions.hint: Poorly trained clergy was a major problem Trent set out to fix through formal training.

citations.quote: [Each church shall] maintain, educate religiously, and train in ecclesiastical discipline a certain number of youths of their city and diocese.

questions.prompt: True or False: In 1566, Trent's Roman Catechism was published chiefly for parish priests, not for children meeting the faith for the first time.
questions.explanation: True. The Roman Catechism, or Catechism of the Council of Trent, was written as a resource for pastors preaching and instructing others -- its tone assumes a reader who must explain the faith to others, not one meeting it for the first time.
questions.hint: Consider who most needed a reliable, standardized reference in a period of contested preaching.

questions.prompt: Trent-era Rome also maintained an ____ of Forbidden Books, listing works Catholics were instructed not to read without special permission.
questions.explanation: The Index, formally established in this same era and maintained for centuries afterward, reflects the period's real anxiety about controlling access to Reformation-era writings -- a disciplinary tool distinct from Trent's positive doctrinal and formational work covered elsewhere in this level.
questions.hint: The word for an official list -- in this case, of books Catholics were instructed to avoid.

questions.prompt: The Council of Trent's decree establishing seminaries addressed what practical problem in the pre-Reformation Church?
choices: Many parish priests were poorly educated and inconsistently formed, since there was no standard system for training clergy
There were, at the time, simply too many ordained priests relative to the total lay population
Priests of this period were formally and entirely forbidden from receiving any theological education
Seminaries of this kind already existed everywhere and Trent's decree only renamed them
questions.correctAnswer: Many parish priests were poorly educated and inconsistently formed, since there was no standard system for training clergy
questions.explanation: Poor clerical formation was a real and serious contributor to the crisis the Reformation exposed. Trent's seminary decree was not a side note to its doctrinal work -- it was a direct structural response to a genuine failure, and dioceses still operate seminaries built on this decree today.
questions.hint: Ask what kind of training existed for parish priests before this decree.

questions.prompt: Even as Trent was reforming the Church at home, what was happening at the same time on a much wider, global scale?
choices: Catholic missionaries were carrying the faith to newly reached lands in Asia and the Americas
The Church was deliberately withdrawing entirely from any activity outside of Europe
All missionary activity had permanently and completely ceased since the apostolic era
Europe had lost essentially all contact with the wider world during this whole period
questions.correctAnswer: Catholic missionaries were carrying the faith to newly reached lands in Asia and the Americas
questions.explanation: Trent's internal renewal and a real global missionary expansion happen side by side in this same century -- the next level turns to that missionary story directly, including the real cultural questions it raised.
questions.hint: This is exactly what the next level in this topic turns to.
